verses.1: Thus asked by Sri Rama, Hanuman repeated everything spoken by Sita to Rama.
verses.2: "O bull among men queen Janaki related to me as a token of identification an incident that had taken place at Chitrakuta in the past.
verses.3: "When she was lying on your lap happily she awoke early and a crow came swiftly and scratched on her breast.
verses.4: "O Bharata's brother, when Sita awoke from sleep you slept on her lap. The same crow again hurt her.
verses.5: Again and again the crow came to her and scratched her. She woke you up as you were getting wet with blood shed from her body.
verses.6: "O scorcher of enemies pained by the crow hurting her repeatedly, while you were sleeping happily, she woke you up and informed you about it.
verses.7: "Seeing the blood flowing from her breasts you became furious like a hissing serpent and said:
verses.8: "You are of timid nature. Who has scratched your breasts with the tip of the nail? Who is sporting with an enraged fivehooded serpent"?
verses.9: 'Seeing all over, at once I glanced at the crow that stood in front of her with sharp bloodstained nails'.
verses.10: 'That crow, the foremost of the birds was the son of Indra moving about all over the earth swiftly. His speed matched the Windgod's.
verses.11: 'O longarmed, wise and revered Rama, then in anguish you took a cruel decision'.
verses.12: 'You took out a blade of grass from your mat and chanted the mantra to invoke the weapon of Brahma (Brahmastra) and hurled it on the crow. It blazed like the fire of the doom's day.
verses.13: 'You hurled the blazing blade of grass on to the crow. That burning blade of grass chased the crow.
verses.14: 'He was abandoned by his father, even by great sages and gods. Then he went round the three worlds but could not find a saviour.
verses.15: 'O destroyer of enemies the crow came back again to you trembling seeking protection from you and fell on the ground. Even though it deserved to be slayed, you saved him out of compassion.
verses.16: 'O Rama since a divine weapon cannot be withdrawn, it did strike his right eye'.
verses.17: The crow, once released, regained its own abode. "Thus, though you are the best among knowers of missiles, of great being and of good character too —
verses.18: "— for what reason, Raghava, do you not employ the missile against the rakshasas? Neither danavas nor gandharvas, neither asuras nor the hosts of Maruts —
verses.19: "— are able so to contend with you in battle, Rama. If you the valorous have any concern for me —
verses.20: "— let Ravana be slain swiftly in battle with keen shafts; or let Lakshmana, scorcher of foes, receive his brother's command.
verses.21: "For what reason does that best of men, Raghava, not protect me? Those two tigers among men, of splendour equal to wind and fire, are able —
verses.22: "— and unassailable even to the gods: for what reason do they overlook me? Surely some great misdeed of mine alone is the cause —
verses.23: "— in that those two scorchers of foes, though able and together, do not protect me." Having heard the piteous and well-spoken word of Vaidehi,
verses.24: I spoke to her once again: "Lady, I swear to you by truth, Rama is turned away from all but grief for you.
verses.25: "And when Rama is overcome with sorrow, Lakshmana burns with it. Your ladyship has been found at last; this is no time for grieving.
verses.26: "In this very moment, radiant lady, you shall see the end of your sorrows. Those two tigers among men, princes and scorchers of foes,
verses.27: "their zeal roused by the sight of you, shall reduce Lanka to ashes; and having slain in battle the terrible Ravana with his kinsmen,
verses.28: "Raghava shall assuredly lead you to his own city, fair one. And what token, blameless one, Rama would recognise,
verses.29: "begetting joy in him, that you should give me." She looked round all the quarters, and from her garment
verses.30: "loosed the excellent knot of her braid and gave me this gem, O you of great strength. Receiving the gem in both hands for your sake, beloved of the Raghus,
verses.31: "I saluted her with my head and made haste to return. Seeing my zeal made ready for the going, the lady of fair complexion,
verses.32: "as I swelled in size, addressed me, the daughter of Janaka, her face full of tears, piteous, her speech choked with weeping.
verses.33: "Startled by my springing up and struck by the surge of grief, Sita then said to me: 'You are blessed, great monkey,
verses.34: "'in that you shall see the mighty-armed and lotus-eyed Rama, and the mighty-armed and illustrious Lakshmana, my brother-in-law.'
verses.35: "Addressed thus by Sita, I spoke to Maithili: 'Lady, delight of Janaka, mount swiftly upon my back,
verses.36: "'that today I may show you your lord Raghava, greatly blessed and dark-eyed one, with Sugriva and with Lakshmana.'
verses.37: "Then that lady said to me: 'Great monkey, bull among vanaras, that I should of my own will resort to your back — this is no dharma.
verses.38: "'And formerly, hero, I was touched upon the limbs by the rakshasa; what could I do therein, sore pressed by time?
